citations.quote: When standard arithmetic is in effect, the quotient is the result of the arithmetic expression
When standard-decimal arithmetic, or standard-binary arithmetic is in effect
The result shall be the exact quotient truncated to 32 significant digits
When a standard intermediate data item is being moved to a resultant-identifier for which the ROUNDED phrase has not been specified
A standard intermediate data item shall be rounded to 31 digits in the situations listed below
Standard arithmetic is in effect when the ARITHMETIC IS STANDARD clause is specified in the OPTIONS paragraph

cases.reason: The native leg is the same and holds at 2002. The standard leg names 2002's standard arithmetic, a different mode from 2023's. Derived: DIVIDE 3 INTO 2 GIVING Q (Q PIC V9(31), no ROUNDED) under ARITHMETIC IS STANDARD: 2/3 truncated to 32 digits is .66666666666666666666666666666666, rounded to 31 digits on the move is .6666666666666666666666666666667, which Q holds exactly. Observed at --std 2002: .6666666666666666666666666666666 (and the same in Format 4). This is PB5575's defect reaching DIVIDE (report, not a new find). Formats 1-5 of 2002 14.8.11.1 match 2023's, except ROUNDED (2002) vs rounded-phrase (2023 adds MODE IS, refused at 2002 as COBOL0803). 2002 has two arithmetic modes, native and standard (ARITHMETIC IS STANDARD, §2002:8.8.1.3: a 32-digit standard intermediate data item, each operation truncated to 32 digits, rounded to 31 digits on a move without ROUNDED); 2023 names standard-decimal and standard-binary, which do not exist in 2002. The row's standard-mode witnesses use ARITHMETIC IS STANDARD-DECIMAL / -BINARY and are refused at 2002 (COBOL0900), so the 2002 standard leg has no witness through the row. The pinned compiler predates the PB5575 run-time arm (PR #1720 is not an ancestor of 24372b7b17), and PB5575's witness has no DIVIDE statement.

The row's standard-mode witnesses use ARITHMETIC IS STANDARD-DECIMAL / -BINARY and are refused at 2002 (COBOL0900), so the 2002 standard leg has no witness through the row.
